references.text: God promises Moses that He will give him a mouth and teach him what to say—a parallel to Jesus' promise to give His disciples 'a mouth and wisdom' ([ref:2 Mos 4:12|Exodus 4:12]).

Isaiah prophesies that no weapon forged against God's servants shall prosper, and that they will refute every tongue that rises up against them—a promise that opponents will not be able to stand against them ([ref:Jes 54:17|Isaiah 54:17]).
The Lord touches Jeremiah's mouth and puts His words in it, just as Jesus promises to give His disciples a mouth and wisdom ([ref:Jer 1:9|Jeremiah 1:9]).

Jesus tells the disciples not to worry about what they should say when they are handed over, for it is the Father's Spirit who speaks through them—a parallel to the promise in Luke 21:15 ([ref:Matt 10:19-20|Matthew 10:19-20]).
Mark's parallel passage where Jesus says the disciples should not worry beforehand about what they should speak, for the Holy Spirit will speak through them ([ref:Mark 13:11|Mark 13:11]).
Earlier in Luke's Gospel, Jesus gives a similar promise that the Holy Spirit will teach the disciples what to say when they are brought before authorities ([ref:Luk 12:11-12|Luke 12:11-12]).

The council members see the boldness of Peter and John and cannot speak against them—a fulfillment of Jesus' promise that opponents will not be able to stand against the wisdom given to the disciples ([ref:Apg 4:13-14|Acts 4:13-14]).
Stephen's opponents could not withstand the wisdom and Spirit with which he spoke—a direct fulfillment of Jesus' promise in Luke 21:15 ([ref:Apg 6:10|Acts 6:10]).

James encourages believers to ask God for wisdom, and He will give it generously—an expression of God's willingness to grant wisdom to His people, just as Jesus promises in [ref:Luk 21:15|Luke 21:15] ([ref:Jak 1:5|James 1:5]).
